title: 第03章 毒素发作第04章 前厅灵堂
slug: 穿越大乾从病秧子开始蜕变
lines: 自己既然继承了他的一切，用方云逸的身份活着，那么就要去面对这个即将风雨飘摇的家族。
他努力地集中精神，试图驱散脑中的晕眩，感知着外界的动静。
府内的悲声似乎渐渐低沉下去，取而代之的是一种压抑的、令人窒息的死寂。
房间外的脚步声变得匆忙而谨慎，低声的交谈也带着刻意压制的哽咽。
方云逸知道，这是风暴暂时平息后的平静，是那位祖母强行稳定下来的局面。
不知过了多久，门外传来缓慢而沉重的脚步声，伴随着细微的拐杖杵地声和低低的劝慰。
“……老夫人，您可要撑住啊，府内上下……现在都还需要您主事。”是一个老妇的声音，带着哽咽与担忧。
“老身知晓……”另一个声音响起，略带着苍老、沙哑，还有疲惫和悲恸。
似乎是在竭力的维持着镇定，“哭过了，痛过了，日子总还要过下去。”
“逸儿……他怎么样了？这事万不能让他知道……先瞒着吧！”
这是……祖母的声音？房间内，躺在病床上的方云逸顿时感到心中一紧。
随着脚步声靠近，让他心脏在瘦弱的胸腔里剧烈地跳动，撞击着肋骨，带来一阵闷痛。
房门被轻轻推开，发出吱呀一声轻响。一股淡淡的檀香混合着悲伤气息弥漫进来。
老太君在她的贴身老仆，赵嬷嬷的搀扶下，步履略带着蹒跚地走了进来。
仅仅只过了半天的功夫，这位曾经雍容华贵、精神矍铄的老封君，仿佛是苍老二十岁。
银白的发髻有些散乱，眼窝深陷，红肿未消，脸上刻着悲痛留下的沟壑。
她身上的诰命服制已经换下，穿着一身素色的深色常服，更显得身形佝偻，脆弱不堪。
两人轻手轻脚地走到床前，生怕惊扰到榻上“病入沉睡”的孩子。
当看到方云逸竟然睁开双眼，虽眼神黯淡无力，但确实是清醒着的时候，老太君和赵嬷嬷都是微微一怔。
随即，在两人眼中不约而同地闪过一抹抑制着的、混杂着悲伤后的慰藉。
“逸儿？你……你醒了？”
老太君的声音里带着一丝颤抖，她挣脱赵嬷嬷的搀扶，急急上前两步，枯瘦的手掌颤抖着抚上方云逸苍白冰凉的小脸。
那小心翼翼的动作，仿佛是在触碰一件极易破碎的珍宝。
赵嬷嬷也连忙凑近，眼中含泪，强行挤出一丝略带着哭腔的笑容。
“小少爷醒了？”
“真是老天爷保佑……总算……总算还有一点念想……”她的话没说完，便哽咽着别过头去，偷偷用袖子擦拭眼角。
方云逸看着眼前老人强忍悲痛、却依旧对自己流露出深切关怀的模样，心中像是被什么东西狠狠触动。
前世作为孤儿，他从未体验过什么是亲情。或许有原主残魂未散尽的缘故，一股热流涌上喉头，他张了张嘴，想要说些什么来宽慰这位年迈的祖母。
content_en:
Since I inherited everything from him and lived as Fang Yunyi, I had to face this family that was about to be in turmoil.
He concentrated hard, tried to dispel the dizziness in his mind, and sensed the movement in the outside world.
The mournful sounds in the house seemed to gradually subside, replaced by an oppressive, suffocating silence.
The footsteps outside the room became hurried and cautious, and the whispered conversations were also choked with deliberately suppressed sobs.
Fang Yunyi knew that this was the calm after the storm temporarily subsided, and it was the situation that the grandmother forcibly stabilized.
I don’t know how long it took, but slow and heavy footsteps came from outside the door, accompanied by the subtle sound of a cane and a low voice of comfort.
"...Old madam, please hold on, everyone in the house... still needs you to take charge." It was an old woman's voice, filled with sobs and worry.
"I know..." Another voice sounded, slightly old, hoarse, tired and sad.
He seemed to be trying his best to maintain his composure, "I have cried and been in pain, but life will still go on."
"Yi'er...how is he? You must not let him know about this...just keep it a secret for now!"
Is this... my grandmother's voice? In the room, Fang Yunyi, who was lying on the hospital bed, suddenly felt his heart tightening.
As the footsteps approached, his heart beat violently in his thin chest, hitting his ribs, causing a dull pain.
The door was pushed open gently, making a soft creaking sound. A faint scent of sandalwood mixed with sadness filled the air.
The old lady walked in with a slight stagger, supported by her personal servant, Aunt Zhao.
After only half a day's work, the once graceful and energetic old prince seemed to have aged twenty years.
The silver-white hair is a little messy, the eye sockets are sunken, the redness and swelling have not gone away, and the ravines left by grief are etched on the face.
She had changed out of her official uniform and was wearing a plain dark uniform, which made her even more stooped and fragile.
The two walked quietly to the bed, fearing to disturb the child who was "sleeping sick" on the bed.
When they saw Fang Yunyi opening his eyes, although his eyes were dim and weak, but he was indeed awake, both the old lady and Aunt Zhao were slightly startled.
Immediately, a suppressed comfort mixed with sadness flashed in their eyes.
"Yi'er? You...are you awake?"
There was a hint of trembling in the old lady's voice. She broke away from Aunt Zhao's support and took two hurried steps forward. She touched Shang Yunyi's pale and cold face with her thin palms trembling.
That cautious movement seemed to be touching an extremely fragile treasure.
Aunt Zhao also hurriedly came closer, with tears in her eyes, and forced out a slightly crying smile.
"Young master, are you awake?"
"It's God's blessing... Finally... I still have some thoughts..." Before she could finish her words, she choked and looked away, secretly wiping the corners of her eyes with her sleeves.
Fang Yunyi looked at the old man in front of him who was suppressing his grief but still showing deep concern for himself, and his heart seemed to be severely touched by something.
As an orphan in his previous life, he had never experienced what family love was. Perhaps because of the lingering soul of the original owner, a wave of heat surged into his throat. He opened his mouth, wanting to say something to comfort the elderly grandmother.
